lines: This is SANT. It turns a few quick, imperfect human demos into a robot that actually works. Let's walk through it, from the moment the site loads.
The story starts with the problem. Robots learn by copying demonstrations, and they need hundreds. Good ones are expensive. Cheap ones, from a mouse or a webcam, are messy.
So we built SANT: Simulate, Augment, Neaten, Train. Every demo is replayed in NVIDIA Isaac Lab, repaired where physics says no, and multiplied into verified copies.
Nemotron, on Nebius Token Factory, proposes. Physics verifies.
Ten demos in. A tested robot out.
The result: zero out of forty, copied directly. Thirty out of forty, through SANT.
Without the human demos, the same reinforcement-learning teacher never lifted the cube.
And SANT checked the teacher too, and caught it moving too fast.
At the end of the descent, the workshop builds itself. This is where all the work happens.
The shelf holds every job as a cartridge: record, perfect, multiply, train.
Plug one into the machine, and it projects the robot, replaying a real, physics-checked demo.
At the bench, you make your own cartridge: a shell, a colour, a robot, a name.
The wall shows the arms SANT has run in Isaac, and the ones planned next.
And the proof screen steps through how we know it works.
Now, live. Record drives a Franka arm inside NVIDIA Isaac Lab. Down to the cube, grab it, carry it to the bin, and let go.
SANT reviews it on the spot: in the bin, no pushing, one millimetre off centre. Pass.
Scenes can come from a sentence: Nemotron writes the plan, and code checks it.
Run SANT replays the demo with real contact forces, then multiplies it. Every copy is replayed, and only the ones that pass are kept. Ten out of ten.
The test track replays all forty final runs from Isaac. Thirty succeed.
Next, we want SANT to take any robot file, so anyone passionate about robotics can train their own robot, without the cost of a lab. A few human demos in, a robot that works out. This is SANT.
